headline: Five days cold since the last run — the restart pair never became a rhythm. The Åre block still carries the base. Strength and a fresh threshold read remain the two open gaps.
confidence_reasons: No recent activity data in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is defined more by what's missing than what's happening. Two short, genuinely fast runs restarted things after the big Åre trail block, but no third has landed, and the gap since the last one is now stretching. That doesn't erase fitness — the recent four-week volume still sits far above the prior block, and the trail base is deep — but running cadence has gone quiet at exactly the moment it needed a confirming session. Strength remains the most degraded consistency line, with only a handful of sessions in the last month and none recently. Steps stay high enough to suggest real background movement even on rest days, which cushions the running lull somewhat. Sleep and cardio-load figures are too sparse to lean on. The net read: a well-based athlete coasting on accumulated work rather than actively building this week.
sections.trends: The year-to-date distance is dramatically ahead of the same point last year, and the recent four-week block reflects the Åre volume spike more than any steady weekly build. The shape is cyclical-to-irregular rather than smoothly progressive: a huge trail durability block followed by a sharp drop to a couple of short quality efforts. That swing is consistent with the athlete's year-round hybrid model — durability banked, then a pivot toward speed — but the pivot hasn't yet established its own weekly cadence. Nothing here signals regression; it signals a transition that needs a few more data points to read as intentional rather than incidental.
sections.threshold: The threshold number is now the oldest signal on the board by a wide margin, dating back to early summer, and nothing since has tested it. The recent short runs touched genuinely fast paces with real top-end range, which is at least consistent with threshold holding, but a big trail block skews toward durability over lactate-clearance sharpness, so the old value shouldn't be assumed intact without a fresh sustained effort. Treat the current figure as a plausible anchor, not a confirmed one.
sections.zones: The intensity split across recent sessions is cleanly bimodal, and that's appropriate. The Åre runs sat almost entirely in Z1 for enormous durations — proper time-on-feet work — while the two restart runs carried meaningful Z3 with brief Z4 spikes, showing genuine range top to bottom rather than settling in the grey zone. That's a healthy distribution: the polarisation is real, not accidental. The one thing still absent is a deliberate, sustained tempo block — the restart runs mixed easy and quality within single sessions rather than committing to one clear intent.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR history reads as expected for functional work — mostly low-zone with occasional Z2/Z3 excursions depending on session structure — and there's nothing anomalous in the source agreement. The strength HR entries all sit within a sensible effort band relative to each other. Nothing genuinely notable to flag here beyond the plain fact that strength sessions have become too infrequent to build any HR trend from.
sections.calendar: The running streak remains long and intact at the weekly level, but the texture underneath it has thinned: the calendar shows a dense trail cluster followed by a sparse tail. Frequency has effectively dropped to a trickle over the last stretch, and strength has essentially fallen out of the weekly rhythm entirely. The streak line stays green, but the underlying frequency is the softest it's been in a while.
sections.personal_bests: The short 5K and 10K bests from last autumn came off a period of clear speed focus, and the recent fast runs show the top-end is still accessible — but at short distances and mixed intent, not sustained race efforts. Nothing suggests a PB is imminent without a dedicated speed block; the current base is trail-durability weighted. The ultra bests remain firmly in reach given the Åre work, but there's no event driving them.

watch_items: Watch whether a run lands soon at all — the concern has shifted from "confirm cadence" to "restart the cadence" as the gap widens.
Watch for a single committed tempo effort to refresh the stale threshold rather than more mixed-intent short runs.
Watch whether strength reappears in any form — it remains the most degraded consistency signal and has no recent anchor at all.
Watch whether the next running block declares a clear direction (trail durability vs speed) or stays in transition limbo.
